% rhythm: article theorem-like environments: paragraph into a theorem, theorem to proof, proof to paragraph; the markers are the heads the classes generate, which open each block's first line
% boundary: par-theorem Theorem span
% boundary: theorem-proof Proof span
% boundary: proof-par Dogwood span
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\usepackage{fontspec}
\setmainfont{OpenSans-Regular.ttf}[Path=../corpus/fonts/, BoldFont=OpenSans-Bold.ttf, ItalicFont=OpenSans-Italic.ttf, BoldItalicFont=OpenSans-BoldItalic.ttf]
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
Alder is the paragraph before the theorem.
\begin{theorem}
Birch is the theorem's statement.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Cedar is the proof's one line.
\end{proof}
Dogwood is the paragraph after the proof.
\end{document}
